To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the body of the viewer can be used for non-imitative forms of empathy, specifically, transomatizations, that are supported by the body’s empathic, intersensory, and intersubjective capacities, which develop in early life and are grounded in the body’s breathing.
the viewer’s breathing is one of many embodied operations that can be used for a non- imitative form of empathy termed transomatization, which can be applied to the experience of viewing art.

the concept of Einführung as empathy can be expanded to include transomatization, a non-imitation form of empathy; that transomatization is a form of embodied cognition; that embodied cognition can be used to understand the experience of viewing art; and that the experience of viewing Church’s Morning can be enhanced by using breathing as an embodied correlate for the art work.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the body in art and the body as art.
the ways in which viewers can use their bodies to experience art.
the ways in which viewers can use their own bodies to create non-imitative, embodied experiences of art.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
empathy is the breath of art.
the proposed concepts and their application are supported by research in the biological, social and cognitive sciences as well as by first person, embodied, phenomenological accounts of viewing.

the proposed concepts and the embodied experiences they describe are grounded in empathically-based intersubjective modes, and that they are not reducible to the more familiar, cognitive, and representational forms of empathy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the body is an essential element in the experience of viewing art.

empathy is a mode of embodiment, and that the experience of art can be understood as an extension of the embodied, empathic modes of engagement that are characteristic of early life and continue to develop throughout life.

we are attempting to develop a non-imitatative, phenomenological account of empathy that is grounded in a developmental, biological, and social context and that can serve as the basis for a non-visual form of art criticism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
art can be experienced through the body, and that this experience may contribute to an understanding of the art work and its production.
the body, as well as the mind, can be a resource for engaging with works of art.
embodied operations, such as the transomatizations, are not only possible in regard to viewing art, but also are necessary for a full appreciation of the art work.
